title: The $0 Rice Hack: Why I Put Ice Cubes in My Microwave (And Saved $25)
description: Stop eating crunchy leftover rice! Use Mia's simple ice cube trick to reheat rice in the microwave for fluffy results every time. Save money on takeout tonight.
story: I was about two seconds away from opening Uber Eats and dropping $25 on a Thai curry just because my leftover rice looked like little white pebbles. Living in a tiny apartment means I'm always trying to make the most of my Aldi grocery hauls—a massive bag of jasmine rice is basically my lifeblood. The first time I tried this, I actually buried the ice cube deep in the rice, and it just made a soggy mess in one spot. Pro tip: keep it right on top! This trick basically creates a mini steam room for your grains. Instead of spending $25 on a fresh order, I used a knob of Kerrygold butter and some soy sauce I had in the pantry, and dinner cost me maybe $1.50. It’s those little dollar-saving wins that keep my budget on track while I’m trying to save for a house. Honestly, it tastes just as fresh as the day I made it, which is a total win for my wallet and my stomach.
ingredients: 2 cups leftover Jasmine or Basmati rice from the fridge
1 large ice cube from your freezer tray
1 teaspoon water (only if rice is over 3 days old)
1 damp paper towel or parchment paper square
1 teaspoon Trader Joe's coconut aminos or soy sauce
instructions: Step 1: Dump your cold, clumpy leftover rice into a microwave-safe glass bowl. Use a fork to break up those hard, pebble-like white chunks until the grains are loose.
Step 2: Place one single frosty ice cube right on top of the rice pile. Don't push it down into the rice; it needs to sit on the surface like a little winter cap to work its magic.
Step 3: Cover the bowl tightly with a damp, crinkly paper towel or a microwave-safe plate. This creates a seal to trap the moisture as the microwave starts to hum and the water turns into steam.

Step 4: Nuke it on high for 60 to 90 seconds. When it's done, you'll see a cloud of steam rise as you lift the cover, revealing soft, pearly grains. Discard the leftover ice pebble, add your butter, and fluff with a fork.
proHack: Don't stir the ice into the rice before heating! The whole point is for the cube to stay relatively solid while the microwave energy vibrates the water molecules to create steam. If you stir it in, you just get a soggy rice puddle in the center.
storage: Store your rice in an airtight container for no more than 4 days in the fridge. If you're freezing it, use a flat Ziploc bag to save space. To reheat from frozen, just follow this same ice cube method but add an extra 45 seconds to the timer.

faqs.question: Can I use a frozen veggie instead of ice if I'm out?
faqs.answer: I wouldn't recommend it. Frozen peas or corn release starch and sugars that can make the rice sticky and weird. Stick to a plain ice cube or a teaspoon of water if you're desperate.

faqs.question: Why is my rice still hard in the middle after reheating?
faqs.answer: Your microwave might have a weak spot. Try stopping the timer halfway through to give the bowl a quick rotate, then finish the last 30 seconds to ensure the steam reaches every grain.
